defects: r1c1, whole face: identity proportions drift from REF—the face is narrower, eyes are smaller relative to the cheeks, and the nose/mouth sit more compactly, making her look like a close sibling rather than an exact puppet.
r1c2, mouth and lower face: the oversized symmetrical open mouth stretches the jaw and reads as a generic singing pose rather than a controlled 'aa' phoneme.
r1c3, eyebrows and gaze: the sharply asymmetric brow combined with the upward side-eye reads skeptical or suspicious more than thoughtful.
r3c2, eyelids: both lids are parked at an identical half-closed height, producing a sleepy/stilted pose instead of a natural transitional blink.

r3c3, eyes, nose, cheek and hairline: the turn is assembled by sliding features rather than preserving convincing head volume; the far eye remains too large and the nose/cheek perspective is too frontal.
top_fix: Lock a REF-matched neutral head model first—especially face width, eye scale and spacing, nose/mouth placement, cheek volume, and hair silhouette—then rebuild expressions and the 20-degree turn as deformations of that single model rather than independently posed faces.
